nodes.summary: If $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is piecewise syndetic, then for every natural number $k$ the set of pairs $(a, d) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$ such that $a + i d \in S$ for all $i = 0, 1, \dots, k$ is piecewise syndetic in $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Furstenberg–Glasner theorem on progressions in piecewise syndetic sets

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{N}^+$ denote the positive integers under addition. If $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}^+$ is an essential CR-set and $l$ is a natural number, then the set of pairs $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N}^+ \times \mathbb{N}^+$ such that $a + i b \in A$ for all $i = 0, 1, \dots, l$ is an essential CR-set in $\mathbb{N}^+ \times \mathbb{N}^+$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions in essential CR-sets of the positive integers

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{N}^+$ denote the positive integers under addition. If $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}^+$ is a $J$-set, then for every natural number $k$ the set of pairs $(a, d) \in \mathbb{N}^+ \times \mathbb{N}^+$ such that $a + i d \in S$ for all $i = 0, 1, \dots, k$ is a $J$-set in $\mathbb{N}^+ \times \mathbb{N}^+$.
nodes.title: Debnath–Goswami theorem on progressions in J-sets

nodes.summary: If $A$ is a CR-set in a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ and $l$ is a natural number, then the set of pairs $(a, b) \in S \times S$ such that $a, a + b, a + 2b, \dots, a + lb$ all lie in $A$ is a CR-set in $S \times S$. Here $a + ib$ is $a$ followed by $i$ additions of $b$, since $S$ need not have a zero.
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions in CR-sets

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a semigroup and $\mathcal F$ a family of subsets of $S$ with the Ramsey property. Multiply ultrafilters on $S$ by $E \in pq$ iff $\{x \in S : \{y \in S : xy \in E\} \in q\} \in p$. Then $pq \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ for every ultrafilter $p$ on $S$ and every $q \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ (that is, $\beta(\mathcal F)$ is a left ideal of $\beta S$) if and only if $sE = \{se : e \in E\}$ lies in $\mathcal F$ for…
nodes.title: Left-ideal criterion for β(F)

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a semigroup and $\mathcal F$ a family of subsets of $S$ with the Ramsey property. For $x \in S$ and $E \subseteq S$ write $x^{-1}E = \{y \in S : xy \in E\}$, and multiply ultrafilters on $S$ by $E \in pq$ iff $\{x \in S : x^{-1}E \in q\} \in p$. Then $pq \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ for all $p, q \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ if and only if every $E \subseteq S$ has the following property: if there is…
nodes.title: Subsemigroup criterion for β(F)

nodes.summary: For every set $S$, every ultrafilter on $S$ lies in $\beta(\mathcal F)$, where $\mathcal F$ is the family of all nonempty subsets of $S$; that is, $\beta(\mathcal F) = \beta S$, the set of all ultrafilters on $S$.
nodes.title: β of the nonempty sets is all of βS

nodes.summary: For a family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of a set $S$, $\beta(\mathcal F)$ is the set of ultrafilters $p$ on $S$ all of whose members lie in $\mathcal F$, that is, $A \in \mathcal F$ for every $A \in p$.
nodes.title: The set β(F) of ultrafilters inside a family

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a countable semigroup and $\mathcal F$ a family of subsets of $S$ with the Ramsey property. For $x \in S$ and $E \subseteq S$ write $x^{-1}E = \{y \in S : xy \in E\}$, multiply ultrafilters on $S$ by $E \in pq$ iff $\{x \in S : x^{-1}E \in q\} \in p$, and assume $pq \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ for all $p, q \in \beta(\mathcal F)$. If $A \subseteq S$ belongs to some $p \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ with $pp = p$ (an…
nodes.title: Essential F-sets contain shift-closed decreasing sequences (countable case)

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a semigroup and $\mathcal F$ a family of subsets of $S$ with the Ramsey property, and multiply ultrafilters on $S$ by $E \in pq$ iff $\{x \in S : \{y \in S : xy \in E\} \in q\} \in p$. If $pq \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ for all $p, q \in \beta(\mathcal F)$, then there is $p \in \beta(\mathcal F)$ with $pp = p$.
nodes.title: β(F) contains an idempotent when it is a subsemigroup

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a semigroup and let $F$ be a family of subsets of $S$ with the Ramsey property, and write $\beta(F)$ for the set of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $F$. For $x \in S$ and $E \subseteq S$ write $x^{-1}E = \{y \in S : xy \in E\}$, and multiply ultrafilters on $S$ by the rule that $E \in p \cdot q$ if and only if $\{x \in S : x^{-1}E \in q\} \in p$. Suppose that $p \cdot q \in \beta(F)$…
nodes.title: Decreasing shift-closed sequences give essential sets

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a nonempty commutative semigroup, then $S$ itself is a piecewise syndetic subset of $S$.
nodes.title: The whole commutative semigroup is piecewise syndetic

nodes.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ is piecewise syndetic when there is a finite set $F \subseteq S$ such that the union $\bigcup_{t \in F} (-t + A)$ is thick, where $-t + A = \{s \in S : t + s \in A\}$.
nodes.title: Piecewise syndetic set in a commutative semigroup

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a nonempty commutative semigroup, then $S$ itself is a thick subset of $S$.
nodes.title: The whole commutative semigroup is thick

nodes.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ is thick when for every finite set $E \subseteq S$ there is an $x \in S$ with $E + x \subseteq A$, that is, $e + x \in A$ for every $e \in E$.
nodes.title: Thick set in a commutative semigroup

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a family of subsets of a set $S$ with the Ramsey property. Then the set $\beta(F)$ of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $F$ is closed in the space $\beta S$ of all ultrafilters on $S$.
nodes.title: Ultrafilters inside a Ramsey family form a closed set

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a nonempty commutative semigroup, then $S$ itself is a CR-set in $S$.
nodes.title: The whole commutative semigroup is a CR-set

nodes.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ is a CR-set (combinatorially rich) when for every natural number $n$, including $n = 0$, there is a natural number $r$ such that for every $r \times n$ matrix $(m_{ij})$ with entries in $S$ there are a nonempty set $\alpha \subseteq \{1, \ldots, r\}$ and an element $s \in S$ such that $s + \sum_{i \in \alpha} m_{ij} \in A$ for every column $j \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$.
nodes.title: CR-set

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a countable commutative semigroup and let $A \subseteq S$. Then $A$ is an essential CR-set if and only if there is a decreasing sequence $C_0 \supseteq C_1 \supseteq C_2 \supseteq \cdots$ of CR-sets contained in $A$ such that for every $n$ and every $x \in C_n$ there is an $m$ with $C_m \subseteq -x + C_n$, where $-x + C_n = \{y \in S : x + y \in C_n\}$.
nodes.title: Essential CR-sets via decreasing sequences

nodes.summary: Let $(S, +)$ be a commutative semigroup, and add ultrafilters on $S$ by the rule that $E \in p + q$ if and only if $\{x \in S : \{y \in S : x + y \in E\} \in q\} \in p$. A subset $A$ of $S$ is an essential CR-set when there is an ultrafilter $p$ on $S$ with $p + p = p$, all of whose members are CR-sets, such that $A \in p$.
nodes.title: Essential CR-set

nodes.summary: In every nonempty commutative semigroup $S$, the set $S$ itself is a $J$-set.
nodes.title: The whole semigroup is a J-set

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a commutative semigroup and let $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$. A set $A \subseteq S$ is a $J$-set when for every finite set $F$ of sequences $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to S$ there are $a \in S$ and a nonempty finite set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $a + \sum_{n \in H} f(n) \in A$ for every $f \in F$.
nodes.title: J-sets in commutative semigroups

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a set, let $\beta S$ be the space of ultrafilters on $S$, and let $K$ be a nonempty closed subset of $\beta S$. Let $\mathcal F_K$ be the collection of the sets $E \subseteq S$ with $E \in p$ for some $p \in K$. Then $\mathcal F_K$ is a family with the Ramsey property, and $\beta(\mathcal F_K) = K$, where $\beta(\mathcal F_K)$ is the set of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $\mathcal F_K$.
nodes.title: Nonempty closed sets of ultrafilters come from Ramsey families

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a set. A collection $F$ of subsets of $S$ is a family with the Ramsey property when $F$ is nonempty, $\emptyset \notin F$, $F$ is closed under supersets (if $A \in F$ and $A \subseteq B$, then $B \in F$), and whenever $A \cup B \in F$, then $A \in F$ or $B \in F$.
nodes.title: Families with the Ramsey property

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a collection of subsets of a set $S$ and let $p$ be an ultrafilter on $S$. Then $p \in \beta(F)$ if and only if every member of $p$ belongs to $F$.
nodes.title: Membership in β(F)

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a family of subsets of a set $S$ with the Ramsey property, and let $\beta(F)$ be the set of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $F$. Then a set $A \subseteq S$ lies in $F$ if and only if $A \in p$ for some $p \in \beta(F)$; that is, $F = \bigcup \beta(F)$.
nodes.title: Theorem 3, part 2: a Ramsey family is the union of its ultrafilters

nodes.summary: In a nonempty commutative semigroup, the empty set is not thick.
nodes.title: The empty set is not thick

nodes.summary: In every commutative semigroup, the empty set is not a CR-set.
nodes.title: The empty set is not a CR-set

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
